text:
ci-bot: perf/regression detected: +12% median p50 latency on smallbatch embedder (batch=2, seq=32) in nightly-3612345600 compared to baseline. dashboard: https://perf.redwood/investigate/3612345678 :rotating_light:
maya: saw this in staging after the runtime merge that bumped cublaslt/libcudnn yesterday. not just CI.
jason: starting a quick bisect on staging machines. hypothesis: cublasLt algorithm picker change.
maya: nvprof snippet from a staging trace (trimmed):
```
# before (baseline)
cuBLAS: cublasGemmEx (alg 1) time=3.1ms
# after (head)
cuBLAS: cublasLtMatmul (alg 7) time=5.0ms
memcpy H2D 0.9ms (extra due to workspace alloc)
```
achel: that aligns with what I saw in profiler: kernel changed and we now see an extra workspace alloc+copy which amplifies for small batches. Large-batch numbers improved.
priya: which exact deps were bumped in the merge? can someone paste the PR?
nate: PR was "deps: bump cublaslt to 3.5.2 and tweak selector heuristic" landed by infra-bot ~18h ago. commit 9f4b7c6.
ci-bot: bisect result -> culprit commit 9f4b7c6 (infra-bot) Description: "bump cublaslt; selector: prefer alg with lower workspace_ratio".
jason: repro steps I'm using locally:
```
./bench --model small-embed --batch 2 --seq 32 --iters 200 --trace nvtx > trace.log
# compare baseline commit abc123 vs HEAD
```

maya: quick nsight flame sample:
```
0.000s - memcopy H2D (workspace) 0.85ms
0.850s - cublasLtMatmul_alg7 grid 5.0ms
```
achel: the selector tweak reduced the workspace threshold so the picker now favors alg7 with less theoretical GEMM ops but more copies for our small shapes. autotuner didn't pick this because it's a heuristic change at lib level.
priya: options: (1) revert the selector tweak in our runtime (force prefer algorithms that avoid extra device-host copies for smallbatch), (2) pin cublaslt to previous version in infra images, (3) add a runtime flag to preserve old behavior + test.
jason: I can prototype a runtime guard that prefers algs with no workspace-copy for batch<=4. cheap change.
maya: let's avoid full revert if we can patch runtime — large-batch perf was improved by the bump and customers might expect that. we should land a targeted guard and then roll forward the dep.
nate: ops perspective: if we need immediate rollback for rollout window, we can pin images for next deploy. prefer code fix first then pin as fallback.
priya: I'll open a PR for runtime guard + perf unit test and add an emergency flag to pin old behavior. assigning @jason for review. PR description will reference commit 9f4b7c6 and include perf numbers.
ci-bot: created ticket PERF-8732 and linked regression dashboard.
maya: thanks — can we also add a short perf alert that compares kernel names (cublasGemmEx vs cublasLtMatmul) for smallbatch smoke tests? that would catch future shifts.
rachel: yes adding a kernel-name check to nightly perf CI makes sense. i'll add it to the perf harness.
priya: plan: PR runtime-guard -> bench numbers -> merge -> monitor next nightly. if numbers don't recover, pin infra images.
jason: working on patch, will drop a draft in the thread and post perf numbers. :thumbsup:
maya: ack. tagging @nate for rollout scheduling if we need a short rollback window.
nate: noted, will standby.
